I farm only 6 mu, but I have 30 years of experience, good literacy, and well irrigation, so I do not run my land loosely. I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all 6.0 mu because that is the most stable way for me to use the land, labor, and water through the year. For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than old saved seed because I want stable emergence, uniform plants, and better disease resistance. I will fertilize wheat at a moderate-to-high level because my irrigation lets me turn fertilizer into yield, but I will not push it too hard and risk lodging or wasted input. I will irrigate wheat three times, because in Hebei wheat responds clearly to timely water. I will use rotary tillage for wheat because on my scale it is practical and gives me a clean seedbed. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed on the same 6.0 mu after wheat harvest because hybrid maize gives me the most dependable yield. I will keep maize fertilizer slightly heavier on nitrogen and potassium, use fewer irrigations than wheat, and use no-tillage planting after wheat so I can save time, protect moisture, and turn the crop around quickly. I will spray pesticides only as needed but I still plan for two applications per crop, because clean fields and timely control matter more than rescue treatments later. Overall, I am aiming for steady output and manageable risk, not extreme input chasing extreme yield.
